basic_info.name: BloodGPT
basic_info.category: AI lab-result interpreter (B2B white-label for labs/clinics + B2C subscription)
basic_info.country: Cyprus-incorporated healthtech startup; team operates in Poland (won The Ventures Poland 2025) with CEO Jonathan Kron London-based (ex-(med)24) [uncertain]
basic_info.stage: Early-stage startup: $1M seed raised at ~$10M valuation (2024 per SignalBase/Tech Funding News); still pre-scale — ~500 paying consumer subscribers reported
basic_info.pricing_model: Multi-tier SaaS. B2C: Individual $9.99/mo (1 profile, 10 uploads/mo); Family $13.99/mo (4 profiles); Big Family $17.99/mo (10 profiles); annual billing marketed as ~70% off ('8 months free'). Doctors: $79.99/mo or $800/yr (1 account, 100 analyses/mo, unlimited patient profiles). Labs: manual-upload portal $195/mo + $0.05/analyzed biomarker (5,000 biomarker signup bonus); full API automation $690/mo + $0.01-0.05/biomarker volume-based (20,000 bonus); white-label portals and on-premise deployment at custom pricing. A 'PDF Reports Plan' at $159.99/mo also appears in some listings. No recent price-change history found.
basic_info.target_user: Primary: diagnostic laboratories and clinics (white-label, API, on-prem). Secondary: doctors/small practices ($79.99 tier). Tertiary: consumers and families (B2C) — weakest leg, ~500 paying subs.
basic_info.scale_metrics: Self-reported: 500+ paying consumer subscribers; $1M seed at $10M valuation; 'live in 2 weeks' implementation claim; Trustpilot shows only 3 reviews (4 stars) and an F6S complaint alleging no support/refund — consumer traction is noise-level. No named lab clients or case studies published; B2B pipeline depth unverifiable. Durable threat = distribution model (white-label inside labs), not current revenue.

product.core_features: Upload any lab report (PDF/JPG/manual) for instant multi-view AI interpretation; risk identification in context of test history, age and physical indicators; smart recommendations (supplements, sleep, stress, personalized diet plans); longitudinal biomarker trend tracking with normalized names/units and historical data recognition; smart follow-ups with re-test recommendations and test-preparation guidance; 80+ languages (also marketed as 98); doctor tier adds branded PDF reports (custom logo/signature, control over patient-facing info), online link sharing, AI clarifications, context-aware add-on panel recommendations; labs tier adds white-label portals, branded headers/disclaimers, REST API, HL7/FHIR LIS integration, on-premise deployment.
product.signature_differentiator: Deterministic multi-agent architecture: three specialized LLMs wrapped around a deterministic pipeline for value extraction and threshold logic, marketed as 'same input, same output' — a consistency guarantee most LLM interpreters cannot claim. Paired with a B2B embedding strategy no consumer rival matches: direct LIS connection (HL7/FHIR), per-biomarker API pricing, and an on-prem option where 'we don't store, copy, or access patient information' — a data-sovereignty pitch aimed at European labs. Marketing claims 'First AI to score 100% on Stanford's medical AI test' (self-run, methodology unpublished).
product.lab_data_handling: Pure software layer over existing labs — no own testing, hardware, or lab partnership network on the consumer side. Ingestion: consumer PDF/image/manual upload; doctors upload HL7/PDF/CSV without LIS integration; labs get automated XML/JSON/CSV/PDF/JPG feeds plus HL7/FHIR LIS piping. No wearable, CGM, or at-home testing cadence — retest loop is software-only ('smart follow-ups' with re-test recommendations and prep guidance).
product.family_dependents_depth: Shallow. Family is a billing construct: Family plan = up to 4 profiles, Big Family = up to 10, each with its own monthly uploads, 'track progress together with shared insights.' No pediatric reference ranges, no caregiver mode, no hereditary-risk logic mentioned anywhere on the site [uncertain — absence of evidence]. This is the same gap US players have, and a pillar Dr. Exame can own in BR.
product.doctor_sharing: Doctor-centric white-label: branded patient PDFs with custom logo/signature, clinician control over what patients see, share via online link or PDF, clinician review-and-approval workflow before release, longitudinal tracking across visits, follow-up nudges to bring patients back. Positioned as 'your brand, our AI.' No SOAP note or consultation-brief concept — reports are lab-interpretation artifacts, not visit preparation [uncertain].
product.action_loop_monetization: Thin. Post-interpretation output is educational: supplement/sleep/stress/diet recommendations — no supplement storefront, no telemedicine, no prescriptions, no marketplace found [uncertain]. The real action loop is B2B: context-aware add-on panel recommendations drive lab revenue (upsell more tests), and follow-up re-test recommendations drive volume back to the lab that deployed it — BloodGPT monetizes the lab's testing loop, not the patient's purchase loop.

technology.ai_approach: Multi-agent system of three specialized LLMs with a deterministic pipeline for value extraction and threshold logic; consistency claim 'same input, same output'; described as trained on clinical guidelines and scientific research; customer data never used to train models. Reports include 'transparent medical reasoning and hypotheses.'
technology.data_inputs: Lab reports (PDF/JPG/manual entry); lab-side automated feeds (XML/JSON/CSV/PDF/JPG); contextual inputs: test history, age, 'physical indicators' (undefined). No wearables, genomics, CGM, or structured questionnaire intake found [uncertain].
technology.data_interoperability: Strongest axis — the moat. Exhaust/ingest surfaces: REST API (HL7/FHIR/CSV outputs), direct LIS connection via HL7 + FHIR, JSON+PDF delivery or portal-only, white-label web portals for labs/clinicians/patients, on-prem deployment inside the customer's infrastructure. Cloud partners: InterSystems, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud. Compliance surfaces: HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, subprocessors list, Trust Center. Not present: Apple Health Records, Health Connect, WhatsApp, RNDS/REL (no Brazil surface at all).
technology.platform: Web app (app.bloodgpt.com) plus separate patient/clinician/lab portals and developer API. No native iOS/Android app found [uncertain].

ux.onboarding: Consumer: sign up, upload any lab report, get an instant visual breakdown — value in minutes, no lab binding required. B2B: sandbox access within 48 hours, free pilot, 'live in 2 weeks' claim, setup of branded report styles in ~3 minutes.
ux.data_visualization: Multi-view AI reports with 'clear visual breakdown' of results; biomarkers grouped by panel for readability; longitudinal trend tracking with historical data recognition and normalized biomarker names/units across labs. No published screenshots of scores/indices (no health-score concept evident).
ux.engagement_channel: Weak/transactional: follow-up test reminders and re-test recommendations are the only visible retention mechanics. No community, streaks, WhatsApp, push channel, or content loop found [uncertain]. Classic lab-report-app pattern: user opens on result, then churns — nothing observed that fixes it.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Benchmark credibility is marketing-grade: 'First AI to Score 100% on Stanford's Medical Test' refers to Stanford's test for AI medical agents (MedAgentBench family, NEJM AI 2025 — where the best published model, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, scored 69.67%); BloodGPT's run was self-administered with no published methodology, task count, or peer review. 'Independent FDA regulatory review' is a review, not a clearance/approval; details unpublished. No peer-reviewed accuracy study found. Positives: 'in-house medical experts and advisors' (unnamed), transparent itemized pricing, HIPAA/GDPR/SOC 2 claims, data-never-trained-on pledge, Trust Center and subprocessor disclosure. Social proof is thin-to-negative: 3 Trustpilot reviews; an F6S 'scam' complaint (no service/support/refund).
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Wellness/clinical-decision-support positioning, not an FDA-cleared device; leans on compliance infrastructure (HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, HL7/FHIR) and an on-prem 'we never touch your data' deployment option for risk-averse EU labs. Publishes FDA-guidance commentary in blog. Makes aggressive accuracy claims without device status — the exact posture regulators are tightening on. Zero ANVISA/LGPD/Brazil exposure; disclaimers are configurable per white-label customer.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they do NOT do (Dr. Exame openings): no Brazil presence, no LGPD/ANVISA posture, no native mobile app, no WhatsApp engagement (BR retention channel), family = profile count only (no pediatric ranges, caregiver mode, or hereditary risk), no doctor-consultation brief/SOAP, no action-loop monetization (telemedicine, supplements marketplace), no wearables/Health Connect/Apple Health ingestion, consumer traction near zero. What works (inspiration, not copy): deterministic pipeline for reproducible outputs; per-biomarker usage-based API pricing; white-label with logo/signature and clinician control of patient-facing content; add-on panel recommendations as lab revenue argument; on-prem data-sovereignty deployment; 48h sandbox + free pilot + 'live in 2 weeks' speed; multilingual (80-98 languages) out of the box.
trust_gaps.relevance: Medium. Confirms the task thesis: BloodGPT wins B2B (white-label, LIS/FHIR, on-prem, per-biomarker pricing) while its patient-facing side is weak (~500 subs, no mobile app, transactional UX, thin trust signals). Direct threat to Dr. Exame today is low (no BR footprint, no Portuguese-BR localization strategy, English-first go-to-market), but it is the template a Brazilian lab chain (Dasa/ Fleury/ Sabin) could buy or copy — the defensive answer is owning the patient relationship (family depth, doctor sharing, WhatsApp retention) before white-label AI becomes a lab commodity.
